Change c0439. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. V; 1831 Ch. XXII.

Context before (unchanged): My letter was calm and affectionate.

1818 text: "I fear, my beloved girl," I said, "little happiness remains for us on earth; yet all that I may one day enjoy is concentered in you.

1831 text: "I fear, my beloved girl," I said, "little happiness remains for us on earth; yet all that I may one day enjoy is centred in you.

Diff: " I fear, my beloved girl, " I said, " little happiness remains for us on earth; yet all that I may one day enjoy is [-concentered-] {+centred+} in you.

Context after (unchanged): Chase away your idle fears; to you alone do I consecrate my life, and my endeavours for contentment.

result.rationale: "concentered" becomes "centred": the same verb, with the same meaning; the change is orthographic/lexical variant (a shorter form of the same word), with no change in sense or content.
